citeAs: Seamless Communication, Barrault, L., Chung, Y.-A., Coria Meglioli, M., Dale, D., Dong, N., Duquenne, P.-A., et al. (2023). SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation. arXiv:2308.11596.
creator: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault, Yu-An Chung, Mariano Coria Meglioli, David Dale, Ning Dong, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Hady Elsahar, Hongyu Gong, Kevin Heffernan, and others (Meta AI)
description: A speaker embedding variant of SeamlessAlign for the English-Hindi language pair, derived using the XLSR-2B model. SeamlessAlign is the largest open dataset for multimodal translation, totaling 470,000 hours of automatically aligned speech translations across 37 languages, created through parallel data mining using SONAR embeddings. This subset focuses on English (enA) and Hindi (hiA) speech alignments with speaker embeddings extracted via XLSR-2B.
name: SeamlessAlign (English-Hindi speaker embedding subset, XLSR-2B)
rai:dataBiases: Gender representation analysis showed masculine lexica are overrepresented compared to feminine in the mined SeamlessAlign training data (shown in Figure 23). The dataset is derived from web-crawled audio, which may reflect existing societal biases. Hindi is categorized as a medium-resource language (between 500-1000 hours of supervision), meaning coverage may be uneven. The LID model showed some confusion between closely related languages, which could introduce noise. Mining was performed globally (not locally), which may miss domain-specific parallel content.
rai:dataCollection: SeamlessAlign was created through automated parallel data mining. Starting with 4 million hours of raw audio from publicly available crawled web data, the pipeline applied speech language identification (LID), audio segmentation using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) with over-segmentation, and SONAR-based multimodal embedding to mine aligned speech-text and speech-speech pairs. For Hindi specifically, the raw audio was processed through the LID100 model, segmented, encoded with XLSR-2B-based SONAR speech encoders, and mined against English text and speech using a margin-based criterion with FAISS similarity search.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, totaling 4 million hours across languages. For Hindi (hin), approximately 15,118 hours of raw audio were available. Text data was drawn from the NLLB dataset (same sources, cleaning, and filtering steps). Human-provided ASR transcriptions (approximately 150 hours for Hindi) were used to train the SONAR speech encoders.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Dataset released in 2023; collection timeframe for the underlying web-crawled audio and text data is not explicitly specified in the paper.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is automatically mined and may contain noisy alignments. The mining threshold of 1.15 on the Sonar margin score was set after human inspection rather than full end-to-end evaluation. The dataset covers only 37 of the 100 SeamlessM4T languages (scaling to all 100 is left for future work). The mined data tends to produce noisy alignments requiring filtering. For Hindi, the SONAR speech encoder was trained on ASR transcriptions only and performs zero-shot speech translation. The dataset is not intended for certified translations or high-stakes decision-making contexts.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Speaker embeddings were extracted using the XLSR-2B model (XLS-R-1B features from the 35th layer at 50Hz frame rate). A k-means algorithm (K=10,000 centroids) was applied to map continuous speech representations to discrete acoustic units. Mining used a margin-based criterion with k=16 nearest neighbors and a Sonar score threshold of 1.15. The metadata released covers the full unfiltered 470,000 hours (up to threshold 1.15), allowing users to tune the threshold for their use case.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio preprocessing steps included: (1) deduplication of audio file URLs, (2) downloading and resampling at 16KHz, (3) filtering non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model, (4) Voice Activity Detection (VAD) segmentation using Silero VAD, (5) over-segmentation to create overlapping splits, (6) speech language identification (LID) filtering with a threshold per language such that p(correct|score) > p(incorrect|score), rejecting ~8% of data. Text preprocessing followed NLLB pipeline using the Stopes library.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SeamlessAlign enables training of multilingual speech translation systems that can improve accessibility for the 773 million adults worldwide who cannot read or write, people with visual impairments, and speakers of low-resource languages. However, the dataset could also make groups with lower digital literacy more vulnerable to misinformation if misused. The training data was mined from publicly available web sources, and personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated despite data cleaning efforts.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and improving multilingual speech translation systems, including speech-to-text translation (S2TT), speech-to-speech translation (S2ST), and automatic speech recognition (ASR). It supports research in multimodal machine translation, low-resource language translation, and parallel data mining for speech. The metadata is open-sourced to allow the community to rebuild SeamlessAlign and use it for their own purposes, with tunable Sonar alignment score thresholds.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SONAR speech encoders (based on w2v-BERT 2.0 and XLSR/XLS-R), SONAR text encoders (based on NLLB-1.3B), LID100 (ECAPA-TDNN architecture for language identification), Silero VAD (Voice Activity Detection), audio event detection (AED) model, FAISS library for large-scale similarity search, XLS-R-1B (for discrete acoustic unit extraction from the 35th layer), k-means clustering for unit codebook creation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data was mined from publicly available sources on the web. Although significant data cleaning was invested, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated, as acknowledged in the model card's ethical considerations section.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined data, not manually annotated; no per-item annotation count applies to this dataset.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined; no human annotators were used for the dataset itself (human annotators described in the paper are for model evaluation, not dataset creation).
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: SeamlessAlign uses automated mining with no human annotation; quality is assessed via Sonar alignment scores and BLEU evaluation, not inter-annotator agreement.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined data; no annotation platform was used.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined; no human annotation protocol applies.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling for SeamlessAlign beyond the LID filtering that rejects ~8% of data for quality.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described for SeamlessAlign; missing or unavailable data is simply excluded rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described for SeamlessAlign beyond the initial open-source release of metadata.
null_reasons.license: No license is listed on the HuggingFace dataset page for this specific variant; the paper's model card specifies CC-BY-NC 4.0 for the SeamlessM4T models but does not explicitly assign a license to the SeamlessAlign dataset metadata.
